uses: Calendula is traditionally used on the skin: infused oils, salves and warm compresses of the flowers were applied to minor scrapes, small burns, sunburn and chapped skin. A cooled infusion has a long history as a mouth rinse and gargle for a sore mouth or throat. In the kitchen the petals went into broths and salads, and they were once used to give cheese a yellow color. The flowers also yield a yellow dye.
taste: Leaves bitter and salty-sharp; petals milder
energetics: Culpeper called the leaves hot in the second degree and somewhat moist
caution_pregnancy: Safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been established. Not enough is known; avoid. The EMA does not recommend calendula medicines then.
caution_medications: The EMA reports no known interactions. Little is known about taking calendula by mouth alongside medicines, so check with a pharmacist first.
caution_conditions: Do not use it if you are allergic to calendula or to other daisy-family (Asteraceae) plants, such as ragweed, chamomile, echinacea or chrysanthemums. Use on the skin isn't established for children under 6, or as a mouth rinse for children under 12. If a wound shows signs of infection or gets worse, see a doctor.
caution_duration: If skin or mouth symptoms last longer than a week, see a doctor or qualified practitioner. None of our sources describes long-term use.
caution_topical: Skin sensitization (an allergic reaction) has been reported; how often isn't known. Try a small area first, and stop if a rash appears.
garden_harvest_timing: Pick flower heads or petals once fully open and the dew has dried, all summer; dry them quickly in shade.
notes: Not the same plant as the French and African marigolds (Tagetes). Easy from seed sown just before the last frost; deadhead to keep it flowering. It may flag in long hot spells and recover when it cools. Its flowers draw pollinators; the old claim that it keeps pests off neighboring plants hasn't been proven. Grieve notes the flowers open with daylight and close at dusk, and an Italian name meaning flower of every month.
